instructions.content: NEVER use `@latest` or branch-based action references; pin to a commit SHA
NEVER use `secrets: inherit` in reusable workflows without justification; declare only required secrets
NEVER omit `permissions:` at the job or workflow level; default to contents read
NEVER set `fail-fast: false` by default in matrix builds
NEVER use `pull_request_target` with `actions/checkout` checking out PR code
NEVER pin an action to a SHA without a version comment
NEVER guess the version of a public action; use the common-actions reference or look up documentation
NEVER ship a workflow without concurrency control
NEVER deliver a generated workflow or action without validating it with the github-actions-validator skill
NEVER publish a custom action without inputs, outputs and documentation
Understand requirements (triggers, runners, dependencies) and consult the best-practices and common-actions references before generating
Generate workflows with semantic names, SHA-pinned actions, proper permissions, concurrency controls, caching and matrix strategies
Choose composite, Docker or JavaScript actions by need and start from the provided action templates
Give reusable workflows a `workflow_call` trigger with typed inputs
Declare reusable workflow secrets explicitly and have the caller pass them by name
Map reusable workflow outputs from job outputs
Keep reusable workflow permissions minimal
Use `actions/dependency-review-action` for dependency review on pull requests
Grant `id-token: write` and `attestations: write` for SBOM attestations
Grant `security-events: write` for CodeQL analysis
Name workflow files with lowercase and hyphens
Use dependency caching and shallow checkout for performance
NEVER leave jobs without a timeout; set `timeout-minutes`
Clean up with `if: always()` so cleanup runs on failure
Name shared artifacts with the commit SHA and use upload-artifact and download-artifact v4
Use matrix testing across operating systems and runtime versions
Skip validation only for partial snippets, documentation examples, or when the user explicitly asks
Use job summaries via GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, deployment environments with approvals and container jobs where they fit
Search for documentation or use Context7 when using public actions that the reference does not cover
